facts.fact: The World Bank's digital economy diagnostic states that the civil status system is largely manual in rural areas; it gives no date for the statement, so the document's publication month is used.

The World Bank states that no standardised system is used in the civil status offices of urban Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire and that, with no web-based systems, registers are kept at municipal level with no consolidated information; no date is given, so the publication month is used.

The World Bank gives, as an example of uneven digitisation, that of Brazzaville's 10 civil status offices (9 arrondissements and 1 district) only 2 are digitised; no national count is given and no date, so the publication month is used.

The World Bank states that the Government, through the Ministry of the Interior, drew up the roadmap for digitising civil status and that a prototype of a consolidated system has been developed; no date is given, so the publication month is used.

The World Bank states that the Ministry of the Interior has drawn up a roadmap for the digitisation of civil status, to standardise the systems and create a consolidated civil status database; the roadmap's date and cost are not given, and the publication month is used.

The World Bank states that a prototype of a consolidated civil status system has been developed but its implementation in the offices is on hold because of budget constraints; no source of finance is named, and the publication month is used.

systems.owner: municipalities; Ministry of the Interior for the digitisation roadmap
systems.tiers: bureaux de l'état civil; 2 of Brazzaville's 10 offices digitised; uneven in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire; largely manual in rural areas; the 1984 Family Code does not provide for digitised registration and a bill is in preparation

systems.system: prototype of a consolidated civil status system
systems.tiers: prototype only; implementation in the offices on hold for budget constraints

systems.system: biometric database of the national identity card
systems.owner: a private-sector firm contracted by the Government since 2008
systems.tiers: not stated; photos and fingerprints collected and stored digitally; passports are subcontracted to the same firm

systems.system: numéro d'identification unique (NIU) and répertoire national d'identification des personnes physiques
systems.owner: Ministry of Finance, tax administration and Ministry of the Civil Service
systems.tiers: work begun; a further biometric census of taxpayers and civil servants planned

systems.system: link between identity systems and the civil status databases
systems.tiers: none: the document states that neither the identity card nor the passport system is interoperable with or linked to the civil status databases
